explanation: Fires on tokens inside formulaic, highly predictable boilerplate or code: license/copyright headers (': you can redistribute', 'Neither the name of', 'Inc. and/or its affiliates'), repeated identifiers in code (second half of a class name like AVAssetImageGenerator, LMJEventModel), config/SQL keywords. Common thread is a token predictable from a repeated or memorized template; weak on ordinary prose.

Mixed: fires on tokens in structured/formulaic strings such as postal addresses and ZIP code digits, court-case date headers, format strings ('%Y', strftime('%'), pattern '%d [%t]'), Aliyun SDK imports, and university names ('University of', 'Northeast Normal'). No single concept; weak on ordinary prose.

Diffuse: fires on starts of words in Russian Q&A answers (Навер-, Об-, На), code tokens in programming Q&A (start_link, cv::, indentation inside $.ajax calls, URL parameters), and various subword pieces. Loosely tied to Stack Overflow-style technical/Russian text but no clear single feature.

Fires on word-final or mid-word subword pieces that complete a word, often in non-English text (Greek, Turkish, Portuguese) or rare/technical words (ammonium, quadrature, yakuza), plus closing tokens in code (')', '</html>', '</name>'). Seems to mark completion of a multi-token word or construct; weak and broad.

Fires on the second (head) word of a fixed compound noun phrase or technical term, especially in titles/labels: 'REFERENCE POINTS', 'Human Intelligence Tasks', 'Company Tax Return', 'executionOrder', 'rotatable design', 'Media caption', 'television schedule'. Strongest when the token completes a conventional multiword name or field label.

Fires on the first token/byte of a word right after a space in non-English or non-ASCII text: leading byte of split CJK/Devanagari/emoji characters, and the initial letter of Portuguese/German/Dutch/Norwegian words split into a single-letter token (' f', ' k', ' å', ' F' in 'F.C.'). Basically a word-start fragment detector in foreign/multi-byte text.

Fires in narrative text on the token right after a subject or time phrase that begins the next event in a sequence: temporal transition words ('Soon', 'later', 'quickly', 'immediately', 'before') and auxiliaries ('were', 'be', 'was', 'has been') in event narration. Also odd fires on 'line' in tracebacks and 'index' in git diffs.

Fires on subword pieces in the middle of a word that has been split into several tokens, often rare or legal/medical/foreign words (INS-URANCE, zip-ras-idone, Mittwoch-ab-end, ret-rojection, ir-rev-ocable), plus 'West' in 'West Bank' and 'not' in disclaimers. Mainly a word-internal continuation fragment detector.

Fires on the token completing a short phrase whose content is strongly predictable from context, frequent in synthetic math word problems (variable names after 'Solve', '=', 'multiple of') and sports/news phrases ('goals in', 'look on his face', 'ate it'). Fairly diffuse.

Fires on the final subword piece of rare proper names and taxonomic or foreign words (place names, surnames, species epithets: Albertsl-und, albrech-ti, Cakob-au, Peshe-kee, Chay-ka). Strongest on the last fragment of an unfamiliar multi-token name; near zero on common words.

Fires on function words and common words in Romance-language text (Spanish, French, Portuguese, Italian) and some German/Russian, especially parts of fixed multiword expressions ('hacer frente', 'sur moi-même', 'antes de', 'au cours', 'à la suite'). Essentially near zero on English, with weak fires on English 'what/which'.

Mixed: fires on head tokens completing technical/scientific compound terms ('numerical aperture', 'cystic fibrosis', 'amyloid precursor', 'highest common factor', thyroxine pieces), digits inside long number strings, and 'OF' in 'IN THE COURT OF APPEALS'. Loosely a term-completion feature in technical text with unrelated numeric fires.

Fires strongly on 'void' in Java/C# method declarations after 'public static' or 'public' (strongest for 'public static void main'). Weaker offshoots on other declaration keywords and terms in fixed phrases ('systolic', 'OutOfMemory', 'COPYRIGHT').

Fires in biographical and encyclopedic text on prepositions and connective words in career/award phrasing ('graduated in', 'sixth win of the year', 'nine-time', 'retiring in', 'diploma from', 'a remake of the 1959 film', digits of award years). Mostly bio/achievement contexts, with stray scientific-text fires.
